### OBL-023 — Independent security attestation expectation

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Source | AICPA (SRC-027) |
| Authority type | attestation-standard |
| Citation | SOC 2, Trust Services Criteria |
| Locator | https://www.aicpa-cima.com/topic/audit-assurance/audit-and-assurance-greater-than-soc-2/ |
| Source version | TSC 2017 with 2022 revised points of focus |
| Verified on | 2026-08-19 |
| Jurisdiction | NOT-JURISDICTIONAL |
| Applicability | APPLIES-AT-LAUNCH |
| Trigger | A district or state procurement requires an independent attestation for a hosted service. |
| Control family | GOVERNANCE |
| Control status | MISSING |
| Evidence status | NOT-PRODUCED |
| Owning route | Unassigned; sequencing decision required before any launch commitment |
| Review requirement | PROCUREMENT REVIEW REQUIRED |
| Review trigger | Before any launch date is committed to a district |

**What the source states.** AICPA describes an attestation engagement. No certification exists.

**Obligation.** An examination by a licensed CPA firm against the Trust Services Criteria, producing a report rather than a certificate. Type 2 covers operating effectiveness over a period.

**SSLS interpretation.** The observation window is the real constraint, not the audit itself.

**Current phase.** Not triggered. No hosted service handling customer data exists.

**Future phase.** A Type 2 report requires an observation period of several months, so the lead time must be planned before a launch date is promised.

**Required control.** Operating controls capable of withstanding an observation period.

**Current control.** None. No attestation has been sought.

**Evidence required.** The issued report. Minimum method: Independent examination. Nothing internal substitutes.

**Claim permitted.** None available.

**Claim refused.** SOC 2 certified; SOC 2 compliant; audit ready

**Note.** ISO/IEC 27001 certification is an alternative market path with the same character: independent and not yet sought.

### OBL-031 — District data privacy agreement execution

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Source | The Education Cooperative (Massachusetts) (SRC-042) |
| Authority type | procurement-expectation |
| Citation | TEC Student Data Privacy Alliance; SDPC National Data Privacy Agreement |
| Locator | https://tec-coop.org/data-privacy/ |
| Source version | UNKNOWN |
| Verified on | 2026-08-19 |
| Jurisdiction | US-MA |
| Applicability | APPLIES-AT-PILOT |
| Trigger | A Massachusetts district or collaborative requires an executed data privacy agreement before tool use. |
| Control family | VENDOR MANAGEMENT |
| Control status | MISSING |
| Evidence status | NOT-PRODUCED |
| Owning route | Routed to the pilot-readiness work package |
| Review requirement | LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED |
| Review trigger | First district conversation that reaches procurement |

**What the source states.** These are private contract templates, not law.

**Obligation.** Districts and collaboratives require vendors to sign a standard data privacy agreement before tools that collect student personal information are used.

**SSLS interpretation.** The agreement, not the regulation, is what will actually bind SSLS first. Preparing for it is a product requirement, not a legal one.

**Current phase.** Not triggered.

**Future phase.** This is the most likely first contractual gate for a Massachusetts pilot, and it will import terms that exceed regulation.

**Required control.** Ability to answer the standard agreement's data-inventory, subprocessor, deletion and breach questions with evidence.

**Current control.** No agreement has been reviewed and no subprocessor inventory exists.

**Evidence required.** Executed agreement plus supporting inventories. Minimum method: Contract artifact.

**Claim permitted.** None available.

**Claim refused.** SDPC approved; district approved; DPA in place

**Note.** Template version UNVERIFIED at source level.
